title: Deterministic greedy parity: FUSED in-graph vs non-fused host depth sampling
question: Is the 196-frame FUSED continuation (vs 220 baseline) a sampling bug in the fused graph, or RNG-stream trajectory divergence?
method: Both paths forced to pure greedy argmax (no stochasticity): non-fused BREEZE_DEPTH_TOP_K=1 (host argmax; depth steps draw no rng) vs fused BREEZE_DD_FUSED_GUMBEL=0 (in-graph argmax, gumbel noise leaves zeroed). BREEZE_DEBUG_DEPTH_CODES=1 dumps machine-comparable DEPTH_CODES lines (frame, cb0, cb1..cb15). diff over the full continuations.
prompt: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. We are benchmarking the Breeze TTS two model on the Radeon 780 M graphics card, measuring the real time factor of the full generation pipeline from the text encoder through the backbone and depth decoder.

result.diff: EMPTY — all 240 frames, all 16 codes per frame (3840 tokens) bit-identical between the two paths

verdict.fused_sampling_correctness: PASS — in-graph greedy argmax is exactly equivalent to host greedy argmax. No sampling bug in the fused graph.
verdict.frame_count_gap_explained: YES. Mechanism: non-fused stochastic path advances the shared mt19937 by 16 draws/frame (1 cb0 + 15 depth), fused path draws from a dedicated fused_rng so the backbone's trajectory diverges by frame 10. The 196-vs-220 stochastic gap is RNG-stream trajectory variance, consistent with the dab99db multi-seed sweep (194–253 frames at identical build/weights).
verdict.implication_for_gate: FUSED=1 changes the stochastic continuation (audible A/B needed before adoption per ear-gate) but is mathematically and empirically the same sampler. No test-set KL/CE eval required for the sampling change itself.

host_load: not recorded (parity run, no performance claim)
